notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with a blue-and-yellow strip on the left, the flag colours. Older plates hide it. Russia has no strip.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Nearly all coverage is Generation 3 shot from a red car, with or without antenna. No Generation 4 or 2 exists here.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Some of the worst roads in Europe: potholes, cracks and warped asphalt on most rural roads.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Fences and random roadside objects are often painted blue and yellow.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Cyrillic with Є, Ґ, І and Ї, which the large eastern neighbour lacks. Ы and Э do not occur.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Street is вулиця (вул.) and city is місто (м.), differing from улица and город next door.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Mostly square concrete poles with varied tops and diagonal braces; wooden poles sometimes sit on concrete blocks.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Red chevrons with white arrows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian signs have three stripes.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Town entry signs are white.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails and barriers are often painted black and white.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Big rundown Soviet apartment blocks of light grey brick or stacked concrete panels in the cities.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Brick single-family houses with corrugated roofs behind fences, on overgrown unpaved streets.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat or gently hilly, with tree lines beside the road and wide open fields beyond; little traffic, mostly summer.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall poplar trees are common in many parts of the country.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Landlines begin with a two-digit area code per oblast; a third digit of 2 means the oblast capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Hilly, wooded, pine-covered and curvy-roaded, with very little farming.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall Baltic pine forests with orange-red bark near the Belarusian border, on very flat ground.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Warmer, drier land with shrubs and open fields; blooming sunflowers mainly around Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Signs in the neighbouring language appear mostly in the east and south.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Five big cities have autumn 2011 coverage from a black or white long-antenna car; Donetsk has nothing else.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles with a red band across them are unique to Kryvyi Rih, near red-soil iron mine tracks.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Yellow-and-green bus shelters with sunflowers and the Оліс brand appear in Mykolaiv and Kherson oblasts.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: White bollards with a red reflector wrapping round, like Poland's, appear here.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs in Hungarian and linear single-storey villages with orange tile roofs mark the Hungarian border area.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A trekker covers the exclusion zone from Ivankiv to the abandoned, overgrown town of Pripyat.
